jess_customer: Heads-up — since ~2026-03-12T12:03:00Z our payments ingestion started returning garbled outputs and latency spiked. Example req id: req_72a3f. Route invoked: /v1/generate?model=redwood-pro-2.1 region=eu-west-1. Responses were truncated or contained weird unknown-token sequences. Anyone seeing this?

alex_support: Thanks, digging in. We have at least one other tenant reporting the same. Can you paste a minimal curl and one raw response you got?

jess_customer: Sure — here's the request we use (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-pro-2.1","input":"Process refund for order #12345; reason: duplicate charge","max_tokens":200}'
```
And the body we got back (abridged):
```
{"id":"resp_req_72a3f","output":"<|unk|> \uFFFD\uFFFD\uFFFD processed. \nRefund ID: 45..."}
```
It just stops mid-sentence and the text includes replacement chars. p95 latency jumped to ~3.5s.

sam_engineer: Looking at routing logs: at 2026-03-12T12:02:57Z routing_decision for req_72a3f -> policy=latency-led-failover, original_pool=eu-west-1-primary, chosen_pool=us-east-1-backup, chosen_variant=redwood-lite-1.0-q4 (quantized, smaller-vocab).
Log excerpt:
```
routing: request=req_72a3f policy=latency-led fallback=true orig_region=eu-west-1 served_region=us-east-1 chosen_model=redwood-lite-1.0-q4 tokenizer_fingerprint=0x4a9b
```
That variant has a different tokenizer/vocab mapping. If the client decodes bytes with the expected tokenizer, you'll see garbled output.

maria_sre: Confirming: eu-west-1 had a transient capacity pressure (batch job spike + autoscale lag) around 12:00–12:06Z. The autoscaler didn't provision fast enough because the spot pool had churn. Also a brief network egress congestion increased p95. We triggered failover per policy.

alex_support: Repro steps we've used in support: 1) send the curl above pinned to redwood-pro-2.1 route; 2) when eu-west is under load, runtime may fallback and serve redwood-lite-1.0-q4 which yields garbled text. Observed client decode errors and missing instructions (refund details omitted).

sam_engineer: Root cause summary: fallback selected an incompatible variant (different tokenizer + lower capability). This produces two failure modes: (1) decoding artifacts due to mismatched tokenizers, (2) capability regression for instruction-heavy prompts (shorter, less precise outputs).

jess_customer: This directly broke our refunds pipeline — some refunds were not issued automatically. We need remediation ASAP and a rollback path. Also will need a billing review since we retried many calls.

alex_support: Immediate mitigations we can apply now: 
- Pin your route to redwood-pro-2.1 (disables fallback).
- Add a blacklist rule for redwood-lite-* for your org so runtime won't route to incompatible variants.
- If you want failover, add a fallback compatibility mapping that only allows variants with matching tokenizer_fingerprint.
Do you want us to apply the pin and blacklist now?

jess_customer: Please pin now. Also open an incident and billing ticket.

alex_support: Done — pinned route for acct-lumen to redwood-pro-2.1 and added temporary blacklist. Created incident INC-2026-211 and billing ticket BILL-2026-782. Exported logs for audit (attached to tickets).

sam_engineer: On the runtime side I'll push a short-term safety check: before executing fallback, verify tokenizer_fingerprint equality; if mismatch, abort fallback and either queue to the original pool or return controlled 503 with 'fallback_incompatible' code. Proposed flag: route.allow_incompatible_fallback=false (default false for orgs that opt-in). Plan: small rollout to canary clusters, ETA ~2 hours to prod.

maria_sre: eu-west autoscale: working on adding a burst policy to handle batch job spikes; ETA 25 minutes to have extra capacity. After that we can safely re-enable failovers for the affected route.

sam_engineer: Workaround curl to pin route (for support/ops):
```bash
# patch route to pin model and disable fallback
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routes/acct-lumen
  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx"
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-pro-2.1","fallback_policy":"none"}'
```

deploy_bot: autoscaler: scale-up requested for eu-west-1 by maria_sre at 2026-03-12T12:04:10Z; instance_pool +4 nodes (provisioning).

alex_support: I'll keep monitoring and will post when eu-west is back to steady p95. Sam, please follow up here with the rollout notes for the tokenizer check. Jess, we have the incident and billing tickets — support will coordinate updates with you.

jess_customer: Thanks all. Appreciate the quick action. Please confirm when tokenizer-check rollout is live; we will re-enable failover only after that.

sam_engineer: Affirmative — I'll update in this thread once canary is green and we push to prod.

alex_support: closing loop for now — temporary pin in place, tickets logged. Will keep thread open until sam confirms runtime change and maria confirms autoscale stable.
